items.title: The Company Behind Ugly Gold Phones Is Now Making Ugly Gold Smart Glasses
items.excerpt: Caviar has turned Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses into a $6,840 limited edition called Odyssey, with 24-karat gold accents and an alligator-skin case in a run of 24 pairs. It is the first real test of whether AI eyewear can be treated as a luxury-design object rather than a gadget.

items.title: Pixel 11, 11 Pro, and 11 Pro Fold Hands-On: Better Cameras and Gemini, Gemini, Gemini
items.excerpt: Hands-on with Google's Pixel 11 line, where nearly every new hardware feature is framed as a delivery vehicle for Gemini Intelligence running on the Tensor G6. The cameras, the keyboard and the notification layer are all rebuilt around on-device models.

items.title: Google's Pixel Watch 5 Keeps the Same Design and Leans Harder Into Health
items.excerpt: Google kept the Pixel Watch's round industrial design untouched for a third generation and put all the new work into Gemini-powered health sensing, including blood-pressure trends and insulin-resistance tracking. It is a case study in shipping AI capability without redesigning the object.

items.title: Siri AI is coming to newer Apple devices only, here's the full list
items.excerpt: Apple's rebuilt Siri AI, shipping this fall with iOS 27, requires 12GB of unified memory for its on-device model, cutting off most of the installed base. The full compatibility list shows how hard on-device AI is drawing a line through Apple's hardware lineup.

items.title: HomePod mini 2: Release date, features, price, and rumors
items.excerpt: A rundown of the expected HomePod mini 2, which is set to keep its form factor but gain a faster chip so it can proxy Siri AI through a paired iPhone. Apple's smart-home refresh is reportedly anchored by a 7-inch square wall-mounted hub with a camera.

items.title: The Pixel 11 series is getting its own taste of Gemini Intelligence
items.excerpt: Gemini Intelligence on the Pixel 11 adds task automation that reaches into more than 40 third-party apps, plus Gboard Rambler, which strips filler words out of dictated speech. The AI moves from a chat surface into the OS-level interaction layer.

items.title: The Google Pixel 11 series is here, and the gap between standard and Pro is wider than ever
items.excerpt: Google's 2026 Pixel line splits harder than ever between base and Pro, with the AI feature set now a primary axis of product segmentation. Hardware tiering is increasingly defined by which on-device models a phone can actually run.

items.title: Everything announced at Made by Google 2026: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag, & more
items.excerpt: The full Made by Google 2026 slate: Pixel 11 from $899, Pixel Watch 5 from $399 and a $29 Pixel Tag, all tied together by Gemini Intelligence and Private AI Compute. It is the clearest picture yet of Google's AI-first hardware system.

items.title: Pixel 11 camera gets new main sensors, 'Camera Looks,' 'Instant Night Sight,' and much more
items.excerpt: New sensors pair with 'Camera Looks' presets and Magic Capture, which analyses around 400 frames to synthesise the single best 12MP frame. Photographic craft decisions are increasingly being made by the model rather than the shutter.

items.title: Pixel 11 videography improves with Pro Stable Video, Creator Suite, plus more
items.excerpt: Pixel 11 adds Pro Stable Video and a Creator Suite that pushes model-assisted stabilisation, grading and editing into the capture pipeline. Google is positioning the phone as a finished-video device, not just a camera.

items.title: Google's Pixel 11 phones offer more proactive AI notifications and help
items.excerpt: The Pixel 11's headline shift is proactive AI: Gemini Intelligence surfaces flight status, Maps listings and calendar prompts inside Messages before you ask. Notification design moves from a feed to an anticipatory assistant.

items.title: Pixel Watch 5 hands-on: Health, GPS and AI at the forefront
items.excerpt: Hands-on with the Pixel Watch 5, which runs Gemini on-device so the assistant keeps working offline, and adds an AI workout builder inside Google Health. Wearable AI is quietly moving off the cloud and onto the wrist.

items.title: This is the $1,900 Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold
items.excerpt: Google's $1,900 Pixel 11 Pro Fold pairs an 8-inch inner display with the full Gemini Intelligence stack on Tensor G6. The foldable is being pitched as the largest on-device canvas for multi-app AI workflows.

items.title: OpenAI's first gadget sounds like a tiny expressive AI companion
items.excerpt: OpenAI's first hardware device is reportedly a screenless doughnut-shaped puck you can move room to room, priced around $300 to $400 for a 2027 release. It is the clearest signal yet that the post-phone AI object is being designed as a character, not an interface.

items.title: LG wants to build humanoid robots, and NVIDIA is giving it the brains
items.excerpt: LG is moving its CLOiD humanoid from CES concept toward a real product line, with NVIDIA supplying the robotics AI stack. A major appliance maker treating a humanoid as a home-product category changes what domestic industrial design has to solve for.

items.title: New affordable 3-in-1 smart glasses promise up to 39 days of battery and UV protection
items.excerpt: Rogbid's $69.99 VisionW pairs interchangeable frames with ChatGPT and Grok access, open-ear audio and a claimed 39-day battery. Sub-$100 AI eyewear collapses the price floor that has kept smart glasses a premium-design category.

items.title: Apple Trained Own AI Model for China Market With Help From Alibaba
items.excerpt: Apple built a separate in-house model, with Alibaba's help, to run Apple Intelligence on iPhones sold in China. Region-specific models mean the same hardware now ships materially different AI behaviour by market.

items.title: Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete review: 'this one feels like a necessity'
items.excerpt: A full review of Dreame's X60 Max Ultra Complete, whose AI obstacle recognition and self-servicing dock push the robot vacuum from convenience to appliance. The reviewer argues the machine finally behaves like a household system rather than a gadget.

items.title: I trusted Antigravity and a local LLM with the same office tasks, and only one respected my files
items.excerpt: A head-to-head of Google's Antigravity agent against a locally hosted LLM on identical document tasks, judged on whether each respected existing files. Agentic AI tools can do the work, but only one kept the user's originals intact.
